title: BOJ Lifts Rate to 31-Year High but Yen Slides
content: The Bank of Japan raised its policy rate by 25 basis points to 1.25% on Friday, its highest since 1995 and a fresh step in normalising decades of ultra-loose policy. Yet the yen weakened past 157 per dollar and the Nikkei 225 rose about 1.5%, as a split 7-2 board vote and Governor Kazuo Ueda's reluctance to promise further hikes were read as less hawkish than feared.
summary: The BOJ hiked to a 31-year-high 1.25%, but a divided vote and cautious guidance sent the yen lower and lifted the Nikkei.
context:
• The BOJ has been gradually unwinding years of ultra-loose policy, having lifted rates through 2026 as inflation held above its 2% target.

• Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi appointed reflationist board members earlier this year, sharpening the divide over how fast to tighten.

• A global bond sell-off and rising energy costs have kept upward pressure on Japanese inflation and yields.
happened:
• The board voted 7-2 to raise the rate to 1.25%, with reflationists Toichiro Asada and Ayano Sato dissenting.

• The yen weakened past 157 per dollar as Ueda made no commitment to additional hikes.

• The Nikkei 225 climbed roughly 1.5% as investors judged the overall message dovish relative to expectations.
implications:
• A cautious BOJ leaves the door open to renewed yen weakness, supporting Japanese exporters but raising imported-energy costs.

• Continued divergence between a hawkish Fed and a hesitant BOJ could keep USD/JPY elevated.

• Further tightening will hinge on wage and inflation data, keeping every BOJ meeting a live event for global carry trades.
importance:
• Japan's rate path is a key driver of global funding conditions and the yen carry trade.

• The counterintuitive market reaction shows how guidance can matter more than the rate move itself.

• A weaker yen despite a hike complicates the outlook for global investors hedging Japanese exposure.

title: European Bourses Rally as Rate Fears Ease
content: European equities climbed on Friday, with broad gains across major benchmarks as a retreat in oil prices and steadier bond markets calmed nerves after a bruising week. The Euro Stoxx 50 rose 0.94% to 6,325, Germany's DAX added 0.77% to 25,733, France's CAC 40 gained 0.57% to 8,187 and the UK's FTSE 100 advanced 1.19% to 10,816.
summary: Major European indices rallied on Friday as easing oil and calmer bond markets lifted risk appetite.
context:
• European markets had been rattled through the week by a global bond rout and energy-driven inflation fears.

• The Bank of England held rates on Thursday, while eurozone inflation data reinforced a higher-for-longer backdrop.

• European equities have enjoyed a strong 2026, but rich valuations left them sensitive to the swing in yields.
happened:
• The Euro Stoxx 50 gained 0.94% to 6,325 and the DAX rose 0.77% to 25,733.

• The CAC 40 added 0.57% to 8,187 while the FTSE 100 outperformed with a 1.19% rise to 10,816.

• The advance tracked a pullback in crude prices and a steadier tone in government bond markets.
implications:
• Continued relief in energy and rates would support the region's banks and cyclicals.

• Any renewed spike in oil or yields remains the clearest threat to the rally.

• Sterling assets drew support from the BoE's steady-hand stance amid the broader turmoil.
importance:
• Europe's benchmarks have been among 2026's standout performers, so their resilience matters for global allocators.

• The bounce shows dip-buying appetite survived the week's bond-driven volatility.

• Rate-sensitive sectors remain the swing factor for the region's direction.

title: Wall Street Steadies on Triple-Witching Friday
content: US stocks ended a turbulent week on a mixed note during a triple-witching session, as the S&P 500 edged up 0.17% to 7,650.50 and the Nasdaq Composite rose 0.39% to 26,522.55, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average slipped 95.40 points, or 0.18%, to 51,682.64. The 10-year Treasury yield hovered near 5%, keeping pressure on rate-sensitive corners of the market as the Dow and S&P booked weekly losses.
summary: US indices were mixed on a triple-witching Friday, with the Dow and S&P closing a volatile week lower as yields lingered near 5%.
context:
• Markets spent the week digesting the Fed's first rate hike since 2023 and a surge in Treasury yields.

• Triple-witching, the simultaneous expiry of stock-index futures and options, tends to amplify volume and volatility.

• Elevated long-term yields have weighed on richly valued megacap and growth names.
happened:
• The S&P 500 rose 0.17% to 7,650.50 and the Nasdaq gained 0.39% to 26,522.55.

• The Dow fell 95.40 points to 51,682.64, and both the Dow and S&P finished the week lower.

• The 10-year yield hovered around 5%, keeping a lid on broader risk appetite.
implications:
• With the Fed signalling another possible hike, equities remain hostage to the path of yields.

• Growth and technology leadership is the most exposed if the front end reprices higher.

• A sustained pullback in oil and yields is the clearest catalyst for a broader recovery.
importance:
• The session capped a week that reset expectations towards higher-for-longer US rates.

• Narrow leadership leaves indices vulnerable to swings in a handful of megacaps.

• Triple-witching flows can distort short-term signals, complicating positioning into quarter-end.

title: 10-Year Treasury Yield Camps Near 5%
content: The benchmark 10-year US Treasury yield lingered around 5% at the end of the week after breaching that level earlier for the first time in almost three years, touching its highest since 2007. The monthslong sell-off has been driven by sticky inflation, a swelling budget deficit, heavy corporate issuance and an oil-led revival of inflation expectations, though some investors have begun stepping in to lock in 5% yields.
summary: The 10-year Treasury yield held near 5%, at multi-year highs, as investors weighed a punishing bond rout against the appeal of 5% income.
context:
• US Treasuries have sold off for months on hot inflation, fiscal concerns and a flood of corporate supply.

• The 10-year traded as high as 5.01% on 14 September, its highest since 2007.

• Rising energy prices have revived expectations that central banks will keep policy tight.
happened:
• The 10-year yield hovered near 5% into Friday after breaking above it earlier in the week.

• Strategists warned the sell-off may not be over, while others flagged the income cushion now on offer at 5% yields.

• The move rippled into mortgages, corporate loans and other credit tied to the benchmark.
implications:
• Higher-for-longer yields raise borrowing costs across the economy and pressure equity valuations.

• Fresh 5% entry points may draw yield-hungry buyers, potentially stabilising the market.

• Any further fiscal or inflation shock could push yields to new cycle highs.
importance:
• The 10-year yield is the anchor for global asset pricing, from mortgages to megacap multiples.

• A durable move above 5% marks a regime shift after years of ultra-low rates.

• The tug-of-war between rout and income defines the near-term risk backdrop.

title: Gold Notches First Weekly Gain in a Month
content: Gold edged up to a one-week high around $4,380 an ounce on Friday, posting its first weekly advance in four weeks as a retreat in oil prices eased fears of prolonged inflation. Gains were capped by a firmer dollar, which stayed supported after the Federal Reserve raised rates by 25 basis points earlier in the week.
summary: Gold rose to a one-week high near $4,380, its first weekly gain in a month, as easing oil offset a stronger post-Fed dollar.
context:
• Gold has climbed more than 25% since early 2025 on inflation and geopolitical uncertainty.

• Central banks bought a net 288.9 tonnes in the second quarter, up 62% year on year, the strongest Q2 in World Gold Council data.

• The metal had slipped in prior weeks as surging yields raised the opportunity cost of holding bullion.
happened:
• Gold reached about $4,383 an ounce on Friday, up roughly 1% on the day.

• It secured its first weekly gain in four weeks as crude prices retreated.

• A stronger dollar, buoyed by the Fed's hike, limited further upside.
implications:
• Persistent central-bank buying provides a structural floor under prices.

• A renewed climb in real yields or the dollar remains the main headwind for bullion.

• Ongoing Middle East tensions keep safe-haven demand in play.
importance:
• Gold's resilience near records signals deep-seated demand for inflation and geopolitical hedges.

• Record central-bank accumulation reflects a broader diversification away from the dollar.

• The metal's direction is a barometer of real-rate and risk sentiment.

title: Brent Eases Toward $103 as Supply Fears Cool
content: Brent crude slipped about 1.5% to around $103 a barrel on Friday, extending a retreat from mid-week highs as fears of an imminent supply disruption eased. Prices remain sharply elevated — up around 13% over the past month — after fresh US-Iran clashes around the Strait of Hormuz drove both benchmarks above $100 earlier in September.
summary: Brent eased to roughly $103 on Friday, cooling from recent highs but still up sharply on the month amid US-Iran tensions.
context:
• Renewed US strikes on Iranian targets near the Strait of Hormuz sent crude sharply higher in early September.

• Constrained Middle East exports and regional production shut-ins tightened supply through August.

• Oil's surge has been the key driver of the global inflation and bond-yield scare.
happened:
• Brent fell about 1.5% to near $103.21 a barrel on Friday.

• The benchmark is up roughly 13% over the past month after breaking above $100 on 9 September.

• Easing supply-disruption fears allowed prices to retreat from their highs.
implications:
• Any renewed escalation around Hormuz could quickly reverse the pullback.

• Sustained high crude prices keep upward pressure on inflation and central-bank hawkishness.

• Energy-importing economies remain exposed to wider trade deficits and margin pressure.
importance:
• Oil sits at the centre of the current inflation-yields-equities nexus.

• The Strait of Hormuz remains a critical chokepoint for global supply.

• Crude's path is a leading indicator for inflation expectations and Fed policy.

title: Bitcoin Claws Back Toward $80,000 as Yields Ease
content: Bitcoin recovered to around $78,000, up more than 5% on the day, as a slight easing in Treasury yields and softer oil prices revived risk appetite in digital assets. The rebound followed a bruising stretch in which the token had dipped below $76,000 after the US Senate narrowly blocked the CLARITY Act, unsettling crypto markets.
summary: Bitcoin rebounded above $78,000 as yields eased, recovering from a slide triggered by the Senate blocking the CLARITY Act.
context:
• Crypto has traded in tight correlation with rates, coming under pressure as the 10-year yield pushed towards 5%.

• September has historically been a weak month for bitcoin, dubbed "Rektember" by some traders.

• The Senate's rejection of the CLARITY Act revived uncertainty over US digital-asset regulation.
happened:
• Bitcoin traded around $78,000, up more than 5% over 24 hours.

• The bounce came as the 10-year yield eased from above 5% and oil retreated.

• The token had earlier fallen below $76,000 after the CLARITY Act was blocked in the Senate.
implications:
• Crypto's fate remains tightly bound to the direction of yields and broader risk sentiment.

• Regulatory uncertainty in Washington is likely to keep volatility elevated.

• A sustained pullback in rates would remove a key headwind for digital assets.
importance:
• Bitcoin's sensitivity to yields underscores its role as a high-beta risk asset.

• US regulatory clarity is a pivotal swing factor for institutional participation.

• Sharp reversals highlight the market's fragility in a higher-rate regime.

title: Eurozone Inflation Climbs to 3.2%, BoE Holds
content: Euro-area annual inflation rose to 3.2% in August, up from 2.9% in July and its highest since September 2023, as an energy-led surge kept price pressures well above the ECB's 2% target, Eurostat confirmed. In the UK, the Bank of England left rates unchanged on Thursday, opting for caution as it weighed sticky inflation against a fragile growth backdrop.
summary: Eurozone inflation accelerated to 3.2% in August while the Bank of England held rates, underscoring a higher-for-longer European backdrop.
context:
• Surging energy prices have reignited inflation across Europe after a period of disinflation.

• The ECB had already tightened in response to the energy shock, lifting its policy rate.

• The Bank of England has been balancing above-target inflation against sluggish growth.
happened:
• Eurostat confirmed euro-area inflation at 3.2% in August, up from 2.9% in July.

• Core inflation, excluding energy and food, edged up to 2.5%, with services at 3.3%.

• The Bank of England held its policy rate steady at its September meeting.
implications:
• Persistent above-target inflation limits the ECB's room to ease and supports higher yields.

• The BoE's hold signals a data-dependent, cautious path amid conflicting pressures.

• European bonds remain exposed if energy-driven inflation proves sticky.
importance:
• The data reinforces the higher-for-longer narrative dominating global rate markets.

• Divergent central-bank responses shape euro and sterling direction.

• Inflation's energy sensitivity ties Europe's outlook to the oil market.

title: Fed Hikes for First Time Since 2023, Signals More
content: The Federal Reserve raised its benchmark interest rate by 25 basis points to a 3.75%-4% range on Wednesday, its first hike since July 2023, in a 12-0 vote aimed at containing inflation stoked by soaring oil prices. Chair Kevin Warsh said inflation had been "too high for too long", and the updated dot plot showed the median policymaker expecting one further hike in 2026, a hawkish shift that rattled equities and lifted yields.
summary: The Fed hiked rates 25bp to 3.75%-4%, its first increase since 2023, and signalled another may follow, jolting stocks and bonds.
context:
• The move marks a sharp reversal from the easing cycle that ended late last year.

• A strong August jobs report, sticky inflation and an oil-driven price surge pushed the Fed to act.

• Long-term yields had already climbed towards 5% ahead of the decision.
happened:
• The FOMC voted 12-0 to lift the funds rate to a 3.75%-4% target range.

• Warsh flagged persistent inflation and said the Fed must prevent price shocks from broadening.

• The dot plot pencilled in one more 25bp hike this year, a hawkish surprise for markets.
implications:
• A tightening Fed raises the discount rate on equities, pressuring high-multiple sectors.

• Higher-for-longer policy supports the dollar and keeps upward pressure on yields.

• The path ahead hinges on whether the oil-led inflation spike broadens into services.
importance:
• The hike confirms a regime change after markets had positioned for continued easing.

• Warsh's inflation-fighting stance resets expectations for Fed policy into 2027.

• Rate-sensitive assets across equities, bonds and FX must reprice around a hawkish Fed.
